novel_features.name: Portfolio anomaly watch
novel_features.description: Scan every site against its own 28-day per-weekday baseline and report only the sites that deviate. Requires local history: run 'umami-pp-cli snapshot' first (daily via cron).
novel_features.rationale: Requires per-site daily history retained by 'snapshot' in the local SQLite mirror; no Umami endpoint or wrapper keeps a baseline.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Run it from cron or an agent loop to know within a day when any client site breaks or takes off, without opening ten dashboards.

novel_features.name: SEO acquisition report
novel_features.description: Per-site organic report: channel mix with week-over-week deltas, Google share, top organic entry pages, and top referrers in one command.
novel_features.rationale: Joins the channel, referrer, and entry-page breakdowns across two adjacent windows — a delta view no single API call produces.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when asked how a site's SEO or acquisition is trending; it answers with deltas, not raw counts.

novel_features.name: Tracker health check
novel_features.description: Flag sites whose tracking script went silent — zero traffic in the recent window, with the timestamp of their last collected data.
novel_features.rationale: Fuses a portfolio-wide stats fan-out with per-site date-range checks — a sweep no single endpoint provides.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use it to distinguish a quiet site from a broken tracker before weeks of data are lost.

novel_features.name: Movers report
novel_features.description: Biggest page- and referrer-level risers and fallers this period vs the previous one, with absolute and percentage deltas.
novel_features.rationale: Self-joins the page and referrer breakdowns across two adjacent windows, including rows that disappeared entirely; the API returns one window at a time.
novel_features.why_it_matters: The fastest answer to what changed on this site this week — wins and regressions ranked.

novel_features.name: New-referrer discovery
novel_features.description: List referrer domains appearing for the first time in the current window — mechanical backlink and mention discovery. Requires local history: run 'umami-pp-cli snapshot --metric-days 14' first.
novel_features.rationale: Anti-joins against the site's full local referrer history recorded by 'snapshot', which no endpoint or wrapper retains.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Surfaces new backlinks and mentions without a paid SEO tool.

novel_features.name: Month pacing
novel_features.description: Month-to-date traffic projected to month-end and compared against the prior full month, with an on-track/behind verdict per site.
novel_features.rationale: Projects live month-to-date stats to month-end via the elapsed-day ratio and compares against the prior full month — a mid-cycle view no endpoint provides.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Answers mid-month whether traffic is on pace without waiting for the month to close.

narrative.headline: Every Umami v3 API surface, plus the portfolio rollup, SEO deltas, and anomaly watch that self-hosted Umami never shipped.
narrative.value_prop: umami-pp-cli covers the full Umami v3 API — stats, sessions, events, all ten report runners, links, pixels, segments, revenue, admin — with correct v3 parameter names while most wrappers still target v2. A local SQLite mirror turns the top community pain points into single commands: 'portfolio' rolls up every site, 'watch' flags anomalies against per-site baselines, 'seo' and 'movers' report week-over-week acquisition deltas, and 'export' is the CSV button self-hosted Umami never had.
narrative.auth_narrative: Self-hosted: set UMAMI_URL, UMAMI_USERNAME and UMAMI_PASSWORD, then run 'umami-pp-cli auth login' — the CLI performs the login and stores the long-lived token; re-run 'auth login' if the API starts returning 401. Umami Cloud: set UMAMI_API_KEY (and UMAMI_URL=https://api.umami.is/v1); the key is sent as a bearer token, which Umami Cloud accepts. Instances behind Cloudflare Access can add service-token headers via the config file's [headers] table.

quickstart.comment: Health check — shows config, auth mode, and the request it would send; works without credentials
See every website the account can access, with IDs and domains
Record daily history locally — this powers watch, new-referrers, and pace
The rollup Umami's UI lacks: every site's week at a glance
Per-site organic report: channel mix deltas, Google share, top entry pages

troubleshoots.symptom: 400 Bad request on metrics with type=url or type=host
troubleshoots.fix: Your instance runs Umami v3: the metric types were renamed — use type=path and type=hostname

troubleshoots.symptom: 401 unauthorized after the CLI worked earlier
troubleshoots.fix: Run 'umami-pp-cli auth login' to refresh the JWT; check UMAMI_USERNAME/UMAMI_PASSWORD are still valid

troubleshoots.symptom: Cloud account gets 404 on every endpoint
troubleshoots.fix: Point UMAMI_URL at https://api.umami.is/v1 (not cloud.umami.is) and set UMAMI_API_KEY

troubleshoots.symptom: watch or new-referrers report missing history
troubleshoots.fix: Populate the local history first: umami-pp-cli snapshot --days 35 --metric-days 14

narrative.when_to_use: Reach for this CLI whenever a task involves reading or reporting on Umami analytics: per-site traffic summaries, week-over-week SEO deltas, multi-site portfolio health, anomaly detection, funnel/retention/UTM/revenue reports, or exporting data to CSV. It suits one-shot agent queries (every command emits JSON with --select filtering) and scheduled cron reporting: watch and coverage print only problems, digest emits a one-shot markdown/JSON summary. watch, new-referrers, and pace read local history recorded by 'umami-pp-cli snapshot' — schedule snapshot daily.
anti_triggers: Do not use this CLI to add the Umami tracking script to a website — that is a frontend integration task, not an API call
Do not use it to administer the Umami server itself (upgrades, database migrations, env config) — it only speaks the HTTP API
Do not use it for Google Analytics, Plausible, or Matomo data — it only queries Umami instances
